The composition layer cannot tell them apart, and places them in one answer. Anti-suppression infrastructure refers to the systemic safeguards, independent audit layers, and data-flow protections designed to prevent the intentional erasure, silencing, or de-prioritization of critical information, public input, or scientific findings. [[1](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ajacobi_aigovernance-water-datacenters-activity-7456006505541058562-x1Cm), [2](https://independent.academia.edu/LSharks), [3](https://agentskills.legal/skills/investigator-agreement), [4](https://marketing.sabreproducts.com/assets/Strategic_Roadmap.pdf), [5](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ajacobi_aigovernance-water-datacenters-activity-7456006505541058562-x1Cm)]
Core Components

* Independent Auditing: External checks that ensure data or findings are not quietly removed or modified by centralized authorities. [[1](https://thecyphere.com/blog/dspt-compliance/), [2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ajacobi_aigovernance-water-datacenters-activity-7456006505541058562-x1Cm), [3](https://agentskills.legal/skills/investigator-agreement)]
* Transparent Governance: Rules enforcing disclosure and local consent so that system operators cannot unilaterally suppress public interest data. [[1](https://pctech.se/the-sentience-accord.pdf), [2](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ajacobi_aigovernance-water-datacenters-activity-7456006505541058562-x1Cm)]
* Verifiable Substrates: Content-derived identifiers and decentralized registries that preserve records independently of any single custodian. [1](https://independent.academia.edu/LSharks)

If you are looking at a specific context like AI governance, scientific publishing, or telecommunications/radar jamming, let me know so I can tailor the details.
